prayer_points: Father, thank You for counting me worthy to be used in Your divine agenda.
Father, let my life bring advantage to Your kingdom and not shame.
Holy Spirit align my will with divine purpose daily.
Every damaging decision I have made be corrected by divine mercy.
Lord, let my presence everywhere I go attract favour, progress and victory.
golden_diet: When you align with a divine purpose, you remain divine asset. Genesis 18:17-19
When you cannot control flesh and its affection, you become a liability to the body of Christ.
Greed can turn an asset to a liability. 2 kings 5:20-27.
Obedience makes one a credible asset. Deuteronomy 28:1-2.
God will always remove liabilities. Esther 7:10, John 15:2.
Your inner prompting to divine leading preserves You from being a liability.

weeks.topic: THE PURPOSE MUST NOT BE CHANGED
weeks.memory_verse: “...and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel”. Daniel 6:17
weeks.bible_text: Daniel 6:15-22 INTRODUCTION. Every life has a divine purpose, some purposes are attacked, delayed, or challenged - but they must not be changed. Jealous men plotted against Daniel and manipulated the king into signing a decree but later the counsel of God prevailed.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: GOD'S PURPOSE IS STRONGER THAN HUMAN CONSPIRACY
outlines.body:
In Daniel 6:4, bible says they could find no charge or fault against Daniel. Enemies tried to rewrite Daniel's destiny but their conspiracy could not cancel divine purpose. Proverbs 19:21. Though God may allow human conspiracy to cause:
1. A Temporary closing of doors. Acts 16:26
2. A brief reign of terror by the enemy. Acts 12.
3. Withdrawal of godly right.
4. Banishment to a lion's den.
But God's purpose will be preserved and produce testimony that nations will hear and glorify the name of God.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: GOD DEFENDS PURPOSE
outlines.body:
Purpose attracts opposition, the moment a destiny begins to manifest, resistance arises. But this the assurance of scripture: God does not abandon what He ordains, He defends. Every child of God must know that:
Purpose is God's idea, not man's invention. Isaiah 46:10.
Opposition is proof of purpose. Acts 9:4
God allows the test but controls the outcome. Lamentation 3:37.
God defends purpose supernaturally. Daniel 6:22.
God defends purpose through integrity. Psalm 84:11.
God turns attacks into announcements. Romans 8:28.

weeks.conclusion: If God gave the vision, spoke the word, assigned the calling, God will defended the purpose.
prayer_points: Father, I thank You because your purpose for my life is unchangeable.
Father, shatter every conspiracy, decree raised against me.
Father, let all traps set up to disqualify me from honour be consumed by fire.
I decree that delay, denials and evil intentions will not stop me from shining.
Father, overturn every system designed to silence my purpose.
golden_diet: God will always defend His purpose, His counsel must stand. Psalm 33:11
The purpose of God for His children will survive every opposition. Genesis 50:20.
Enemy may seal your Daniel in lions' den but Daniel cannot be stopped. Daniel 6:16-22.
For the Lord of hosts hath purposed and who shall disannul it? Isaiah 14:27.
There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless, the counsel of the Lord will stand.
Whatsoever God does, it shall be forever. Ecclesiastes 3:14

weeks.memory_verse: “But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense”. 2 Chr. 26:16
weeks.bible_text:
2 Chronicles 26:1-23

INTRODUCTION. King Uzziah is one of the most striking examples in scripture of a man who began well, rose greatly, but ended poorly. His life teaches us that divine success must be handled with humility or it can become a trap.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: GODLY BEGINNING
outlines.body:
Looking at the glorious beginning of King Uzziah
He sought the Lord. 2 Chronicles 26: 3-5.
He was spiritually mentored.
He experienced victories over enemies. 2 Chronicles 26:6-15.
He had fortified cities and strong defenses.
He was marvelously helped by God.
He had innovation and technological advancement.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: PRIDE OF HEART
outlines.body:
In 2 Chronicles 26:16, bible says ''But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction''.
He entered wrong and destructive non-commissioned office not meant for Him.
He crossed the boundaries God never assigned to him.
He rejected corrections. 2 Chronicles 26:17-18.
He brought leprosy to himself through pride. 2 Chronicles 26:19-21.
He was isolated for the rest of his life, his pride brought separation.
A glorious beginning does not guarantee a glorious ending.
King Uzziah died a leper, he was buried separately from other glorious kings.

weeks.summary: Success is sustained by humility, gratitude, obedience and continual dependence on God. When humility is preserved, success is established but when pride takes over success fades away.
weeks.conclusion: A Lasting success requires a humble heart that constantly acknowledges God as the source and purpose of all achievements.
prayer_points: Father, convert every breakthrough designed to destroy me to glory.
Father, please help me never to forget You as my true source of success.
Father, please give me wisdom to handle fame, success and honour.
Father, keep my heart teachable even when I am celebrated.
Lord, deliver me from pride and the spirit of self-exaltation.
golden_diet: The pride of one's heart will lead him to destruction. Obadiah 1:3
God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble. 1 Peter 5:5-6
Let anyone that thinks he is standing take heed lest he falls. 1 Corinthians 10:12
When power comes, pride may follow an un- unregenerated heart. 2 Chronicles 26:16
Covetousness also can set traps for destruction.
There is grace given by God to be humble even in victory and success.

weeks.memory_verse: “Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth”. Colossians 3:2
weeks.bible_text:
Colossians 3:1-16

INTRODUCTION Heaven bound means destined for heaven, it describes a person or soul on a spiritual journey towards a celestial afterlife, it implies being saved, born again and living righteously to reach eternal life. It's a life lived with eternity in mind.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: DESIRE OF HEAVEN BOUND
outlines.body:
Heaven bound Christians should have the following desires:
Presence of Christ: A deep craving for Jesus's presence and power.
Holiness & Purity: Seeking a pure heart and a holy, blameless life (Matthew 5:8, Hebrews 12:14).
Spiritual Transformation: A desire to be a new creature, changed by the Holy Spirit, leaving worldly things behind (2 Corinthians 5:17).
Following Jesus: Walking in His footsteps, taking up their cross, and denying self (Mark 8:34).
Eternal Perspective: Living with eternity in view, focusing on God's kingdom rather than temporary earthly gains (Hebrew 11:9-10).
Love & Service: Working in love and being devoted to kingdom service, helping others. They are in expectation of the second coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. I John 3:3. They look forward to their heavenly reward. 2 Timothy 4:7-8

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: GOD'S EXPECTATIONS FOR THE HEAVEN-BOUND
outlines.body:
Be born again. (John 3:3).
Show fruits of repentance. (2 Corinthians 5:17).
Live with the consciousness of eternity. (John 14:1-2).
Study the word of God. (2 Timothy 2:15).
Be part of kingdom service.
Be prayerful. (Luke 18:1).
Fellowship with believers and keep good company. Hebrew 10:25

weeks.conclusion: A heaven-bound person desires transformation; they trade earthly temptations for heavenly promises, seeking closeness with God and living a life that reflects His will, marked by faith, holiness, and eternal purpose.
prayer_points: Father, plant in my heart a deep hunger for You above all earthly things.
Father, help me to set my affection on things above not to be distracted by this world.
Father, cleanse my heart and keep me pure that I may see You.
Father, give me the grace to endure present trials with my eyes fixed on eternal glory.
Father, help me to see life through the lens of eternity and not temporary gains.
golden_diet: A heaven-bound Christian has a Godly Desire.
The sufferings of this present time are not worthy compared 1with the glory ahead. Rom.8:18
Blessed are the pure in heart for they shall see God. Matthew 5:8
All worldly allures are temporary compared with things of eternal values. 2 Corinthians 4:18.
Heaven bound Christian has a desire. Psalm 27:4.
The conversation of the heaven-bound is not earthly but heavenly. Philippians 3:20

weeks.week_heading: WEEK THIRTY ONE- THANKSGIVING SUNDAY 4TH APRIL, 2027.
weeks.memory_verse: “The secret of the LORD is with them that fear Him; and He will shew them His covenant”. Psalm 25:14
weeks.bible_text: Deuteronomy 29:29 INTRODUCTION. In a world where everyone wants instant access to information, God values discretion and intimacy, God will reveal deeper purposes only to the humble and the reverent. The prerequisite of having deeper intimacy with God is in having godly fear.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: HOW TO CHERISH GOD'S PRIVACY?
outlines.body:
God reveals His covenant progressively, but many are not privileged to understand God's plans and programs.
Let us look at how one can cherish God's privacy.
By keeping your spiritual experience personal, never flaunt your miracles.
Avoid seeking human validation or applause.
Obey first and speak later. Let actions reflect God's revelation not words.
Meditate and pray privately, build intimacy in secret places. Matthew 6:6
Fear and honour God consistently.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: BENEFITS OF CHERISHING GOD'S PRIVACY AND THE CONSEQUENCES OF IGNORING IT
outlines.body:
Let us look at the benefits to enjoy when having fellowship with Almighty God.
Showing of God's plans and covenant through divine visitation.
Protection from misuse, secrets kept in reverence prevent pride, gossip and misuse.
There will be spiritual growth, just like Samuel in 1 Samuel 3, he later led the Israelites for years.
God entrusts more to those who handle His secrets responsibly.

Consequences of ignoring God's privacy
Revealing God's secrets for personal glory leads to pride and destruction.
Loss of trust. It may lead to withdrawal of deeper revelation.
There will be exposure to attacks, it can bring spiritual harm.

weeks.conclusion: Examine your life, are you always in a rush to reveal top secret God has entrusted to you?
prayer_points: Father, help me to fear You genuinely so I can receive Your secrets.
Lord teach me to treasure Your privacy and handle Your revelation with care.
Holy Spirit, guide me in obedience and help me honour You in all I share.
Father, let Your covenant and purposes be revealed to me in Your perfect time.
Lord grant me discernment and wisdom to steward the mysteries of Your kingdom faithfully.
golden_diet: Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God. 1 Cor. 4:1.
Your conversation with God can be face -to- face like Moses.
David and his friends prayed privately before revealing the king's dream. Daniel 2:18
The secret of the Lord is with the righteous. Proverbs 3:32.
Your conversation in the closet with God yields great testimonies. Matthew 6:6
The secrets things belong to God. Deuteronomy 29:29.

weeks.memory_verse: In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. John 14: 2
weeks.lesson_introduction:
Everyone desires a home; a home is a place of belonging, safety and ultimate peace. There are two types of homes; one is earthly, which is temporary and the other is heavenly, which is eternal.
Our focus today is HEAVEN.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: MY HEAVENLY HOME
outlines.body:
Heaven is not a fantasy, but real, promised, and prepared by God. John 14:2.
Heaven is where we will see God face to face. 1 Corinthians 13:12
Heaven is where sorrow ends and joy begins Rev.21:4
Heaven is full of Celebration, heaven is where there is no sickness nor death.
Heaven is a beautiful place made of gold and precious stones. Rev 21:21
Heaven is where there is no darkness. Rev. 22:5.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: ARE YOU PRPARED?
outlines.body:
LIVE TODAY FOR ETERNITY
Colossians 3:1-2 ("Since then you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.") or 1 Peter 1:3-4 ("Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In His great mercy, he has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, and into an inheritance that can never perish, spoil or fade. This inheritance is kept in heaven for you.

Perspective Shift: Our earthly life is temporary; our heavenly home is eternal. This changes our priorities and values.
Endurance and Hope: The hope of heaven empowers us to persevere through trials and difficulties.
Holy Living: Knowing where we're headed should motivate us to live lives that honour God now.
Sharing the Hope: Our ultimate home is not just for us, but a message of hope to share with a lost world. We are ambassadors.
Not Detachment, but Right Attachment: We don't ignore earthly responsibilities, but we hold them loosely, knowing our true citizenship is in heaven (Philippians 3:20).

weeks.conclusion: Your true citizenship is already there (Phil 3:20). So do not fret, when the storms rage, when the bills pile up, when relationships fracture.
prayer_points: Father, thank You for preparing a place for me through Jesus Christ.
Lord, set my affection on things above not on earthly things.
Father, deliver my heart from distractions that pull me away from heaven.
Father, give me grace to live worthy life.
Lord, never allow anything to disqualify me from Your kingdom.
golden_diet: For our conversation is in heaven. Philippians 3:20
In thy presence, there is fullness of joy. Psalm 16:11
Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven. Matthew 6:30.
And God shall wipe away all tears. Revelation 21:4.
Without holiness, no man can see God. Hebrews 12:14.
Blessed are they that do His commandments. Revelation 22:14

weeks.memory_verse: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry. Habakkuk 2:3 KJV
weeks.lesson_introduction:
The most difficult place to be in life is the waiting room: a laboratory, a hospital, an interview, an examination, or waiting on God for a particular miracle.
Our focus today is the WAITING ROOM OF GOD: waiting on God may be one of the most difficult aspects of the Christian life.
In the book of Acts 1, Jesus commanded His disciples to wait for the promise.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: DELAY IS NOT DENIAL
outlines.body:
Our God is the God of times and seasons, Eccl. 3. Therefore, there is an appointed time for whatever he wants to do.
Zechariah and Elizabeth: Their delay in having a child was orchestrated by God so that their son, John the Baptist, could fulfil the pivotal role of preparing the way for Jesus Christ - the Saviour. Their waiting served a grander redemptive purpose.
Abraham and Sarah: Their long wait for the child of promise - Isaac, as described in Genesis 18:10, demonstrated God's faithfulness to His covenant and His ability to act beyond human limitations. The "appointed time" was God's time, not theirs, showcasing His sovereign control over life and destiny.
- The Man at the Pool of Bethesda: His 38 years of waiting for healing at the pool (John 5) underscores the theme that even prolonged suffering and delay can be met by God's perfect timing and intervention. Jesus' arrival and direct command brought healing in a way the man could not achieve through his own efforts or the pool's supposed power.
- Joseph waited for the fulfilment of His dreams and visions despite all the challenges he faced.
God has a purpose for your life. - Jer. 1:5
What you call delay is the season of preparation.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: BENEFITS OF BEING IN GOD'S WAITING ROOM
outlines.body:
- Our faith and character are built. James 1:3
- Our strength is being renewed Isaiah 40:31
- Helps us to fulfil purpose. Genesis 21:2, Acts 1.
- Helps us to learn to trust God. Psalm 27:14.

weeks.conclusion: God has a set time for everything. If it seems like God is silent or hasn't answered your prayers, it is not because He is sleeping; He is waiting for the appointed time.
weeks.weekly_activity: God never delays without purpose. Explain and cite examples in the bible.
prayer_points: Father, grant me the grace to wait for Your perfect timing.
Lord, remove from me every spirit of impatience.
Father, help me to achieve purpose as I surrender my plans and timeliness to You.
Lord, deliver me from rushing ahead of You.
Father, align my life with Your divine calendar.
golden_diet: Waiting builds strength and confidence. Isaiah 40:31
God never delays without purpose. 2 Peter 3:9
You can write your own story of waiting like Hanah, David and Joseph.
God's promise is kept in waiting. Genesis 21:1-2

weeks.memory_verse: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed. Acts 16.26.KJV
weeks.lesson_introduction:
What comes to mind when you hear the word "Prison"? (Physical confinement, bars, cells). Prison is a place of confinement, where one is kept involuntarily or voluntarily.
Prison extends beyond the physical, encompassing spiritual, mental, and emotional bondage, and how our Almighty God is the ultimate Liberator, capable of breaking every chain!

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: UNDERSTANDING THE DIFFERENT PRISONS
outlines.body:
A. The Prison of Addiction:
Someone addicted to vices is in prison.
The craving, the compulsion, the loss of control; It's an involuntary confinement of the will, trapping individuals in cycles from which they desperately want to escape. It promises escape but delivers deeper bondage.
B. The Prison of Demonic Attack/Spiritual Oppression:
Someone under demonic attack is in prison.
A spiritual battle where forces of darkness seek to bind, torment, and isolate. It can manifest as fear, despair, confusion, or a heavy sense of oppression that feels inescapable.
C. Spiritual, Mental, Emotional Prisons:
It can be a spiritual, physical, mental or emotional prison.
Mental: The prison of anxiety, fear, unforgiveness, negative thought patterns, past trauma that re-plays.
Emotional: The prison of bitterness, grief that overwhelms, shame, guilt, a lack of self-worth.
Spiritual: Feeling disconnected from God, bound by legalism, doubt, or spiritual apathy.
These are often invisible, yet profoundly real and debilitating.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: OUR GREAT DELIVERER
outlines.body:
The Almighty God is the God of all impossibilities.
While these prisons are real and powerful, we serve a God who is infinitely more powerful.
A. He Shakes Foundations and Opens Prison Gates - Paul and Silas - Acts 16:25-26
The physical prison shook, chains fell, doors opened.
God can disrupt the very structures that hold us captive - whether they are habits, thought patterns, or spiritual strongholds.
He doesn't just unlock the door; sometimes He demolishes the walls of the prison itself.

weeks.conclusion: Are you in the common prison of life? Surrender ALL your challenges to Jesus, the Expert PRISON BREAKER!
weeks.weekly_activity: Mention some events in the bible that talks about prison break.
prayer_points: Father, thank You for every situation I have been through.
Lord, pull down prisons, and altars; holding back my destiny fulfilment.
Father, destroy every physical or spiritual bondage I am in.
Lord, open by fire every door locked against my progress.
Father, by the power of the Holy Ghost let the chains holding me down be consumed.
golden_diet: Liberty can be proclaimed to the captives. Isaiah 61:1
Before freedom is enforced, darkness must be addressed. Psalm 1o7:14.
Praise can open prison doors. Acts 16:25-26.
Whenever God opens no man can shut. Revelation 3:7.
Even the gate of death opens by the declaration of Jesus. John 11:44, 45.
The midnight cry comes with emphatic response from God.

weeks.memory_verse: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed. John 8:36
weeks.lesson_introduction:
What comes to mind when you hear the word "Prison"? (Physical confinement, bars, cells). Prison is a place of confinement, where one is kept involuntarily or voluntarily.
Prison extends beyond the physical, encompassing spiritual, mental; And emotional bondage, and how our Almighty God is the Ultimate Liberator, capable of breaking every chain.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: STEPS TO FREEDOM
outlines.body:
1) Acknowledge your Prison - The first step to freedom is recognizing where you are confined. What invisible chains are holding you?
2) Cry Out to God - Like Paul and Silas, who were praising God in their prison. Like the man at the pool, Jesus sought him out. We must bring our captivity to the One who can deliver.
3) Walk in Your Freedom - Gal.5:1 Freedom is not just an event, but a journey. Once God breaks the chains, we must choose to walk out of the prison. This often involves steps of faith, repentance, seeking help, and renewing our minds.
4) Stay in the place of prayer and the word for sustenance.
4) Be intentional about not going back to the Prison. Keep pressing forward, and your path will shine brighter and brighter every day

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: TRUE FREEDOM COMES FROM GOD
outlines.body:
Freedom begins with knowing the Truth. John 8:32
Freedom comes by operating in the Holy Spirit's direction. 2 Corinthians 3:17
Freedom is total deliverance from sin's bondage. Romans 6:18.
Freedom comes through service. David freed the Israelites from Goliath by offering himself. 1 Samuel 17.
It comes from loving God and finding Christ. John 8:36
No prison is too strong for the Almighty God. No chain is too thick for Him to break. Trust in God's liberating power.

weeks.conclusion: If you are in a prison today - spiritual, mental, emotional, or physical - know that God sees you, He hears you, and He is able to set you free. Will you invite Him into your confinement today?
weeks.weekly_activity: What are the dangers of emotional imprisonment? Mention five.
prayer_points: Father, thank You for the penalty you paid for my freedom.
Father, I receive the grace to believe you for my freedom.
Every lie of the enemy holding me bound be destroyed.
Every chain of fear, addiction, delay and limitation is destroyed.
Lord, disconnect me from people, places and habits that enslave me.
golden_diet: Liberty can be proclaimed to the captives. Isaiah 61:1
Before freedom is enforced, darkness must be addressed. Psalm 1o7:14.
Praise can open prison doors. Acts 16:25-26.
Whenever God opens no man can shut. Revelation 3:7.
Even the gate of death opens by the declaration of Jesus. John 11:44, 45.
The midnight cry comes with emphatic response from God.

weeks.memory_verse: Beloved, let us love one another: for love is God; and everyone that loveth is born of God and knoweth God. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love. 1 John 4:7-8.
weeks.lesson_introduction: The heart of a helper is a heart transformed by God's love, compelled by comparison, and committed to action, seeing Christ in every person in need. For us as believers, helping isn't just a good deed; it's a profound expression of our faith. It's not merely an action, but a reflection of a deeper reality within us.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: SEEING CHRIST IN OTHERS
outlines.body:
Serving the “least of these” Matthew 25:35-40. Jesus makes an astonishing statement: “Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for Me”
This elevates every act of help. When we feed the hungry, clothe the naked, visit the sick or the imprisoned, we are ministering directly to Christ Himself.
The heart of a helper has eyes to see beyond the outward appearance, beyond social status, beyond perceived worthiness, and to recognize the divine image in every person, especially those in need.
Seeing Christ in others help us to break down the barriers of biases, prejudices and fears that might otherwise prevent us from helping others.
It reminds us that every person is created in God's image, deeply loved by Him and worthy of our compassion and care.
The helper's heart doesn't choose who to help based on their background, but based on their need, seeing Jesus in them.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: HELPING OTHERS
outlines.body:
God expects us to share our abundance with the less privileged. 1 John 3:17, Isaiah 1:17.
When we don't reach out to others, we are limited, but when we help others, we complement one another in strengths and weaknesses. Eccl. 4:9-10, Romans 16:2.
It gives one a sense of purpose and joy within. When you help others;
a. It opens doors for divine reward and favour.
b. It brings joy and fulfilment to the helper. Acts 20:35.
c. It brings unity and compassion in families and communities.

weeks.conclusion: Pray to God to open your eyes to see those who are in need and take a practical step this week to help someone. It doesn't have to be grand; it just needs to be genuine.
prayer_points: Father, give me the heart that feels the pain of others and responds with love.
Father, remove every form of selfishness, pride and indifference from me.
Lord, make to be sensitive to divine promptings.
Lord, let my actions reveal Your love and bring glory to your name.
Lord, raise helpers for me also as I help others.
golden_diet: Whosoever is kind to the poor, lends to the Lord. Proverbs 19:17
Carry each other's burdens and in this way God's love is fulfilled. Galatians 6:2
And do not forget to do good and to share with others. Hebrews 13:16.
Any act of kindness, has a record in heaven.
It is more blessed to give than to receive. Acts 20:35
Spending for others allows heaven to bless you also.

weeks.memory_verse: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father which is in heaven. Matthew 5:16
weeks.lesson_introduction: Our world has evolved over the years, it has experienced the stone age, the industrial age and now we live in the postindustrial or information age. One key thing that came in this age of information is social media. As Christians, understanding times and seasons and how to live and work with it matters, John 17:14-16, 1 Chronicles 12:32. We need to accept that social media has come to stay, the world has gone beyond that threshold and we are referring to artificial intelligence nowadays. Today we want to know the advantages and disadvantages that are in this innovation so as to thrive even in the midst of turmoil in Jesus name.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: ADVANTAGES OF SOCIAL MEDIA
outlines.body:
It helps in gaining access to more knowledge than ever. Knowledge is power. John 6:6, 2 Kings 6:13-23.
It helps your growth.
It makes it easier to connect with people. With the new social apps, you can connect with millions of people from anywhere in the world.
It is a tool to propagate the gospel of Christ. There are many people that may never know God unless we use the media to reach them. 1 Corinthians 9:19-23

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: DISADVANTAGES OF SOCIAL MEDIA
outlines.body:
Although social media is full of advantages for the children of God and for the body of Christ at large, it also could be of disadvantage if not properly harnessed.
Distortion of destiny. Dinah's destiny was distorted due to socializing. Genesis 34:1.
Corruption of thoughts, actions and decisions. Proverbs 4:23, 1 Corinthians 15:33
It can drive you away from Jesus and who alone is the Way. John 14:6, Proverbs 10:22.
It can become addiction, something trying to get God's position in your heart. Joshua 24:23, Exo. 20:3.
It devalues harnessing your hidden potentials.
§It reduces your time of relating and intimacy with your family.

weeks.conclusion: Social media can be powerful, too; both for good and bad reasons; it all comes down to the use we make of it and the goal we set for ourselves each time we are with our devices. As believers, we must not allow this to become a god in our lives but rather an efficient tool for the propagation of the gospel of Christ.
weeks.weekly_activity: How can believers tame the menace of addiction to social media?
prayer_points: Father, help me to use all social media platforms for the advancement of the gospel.
Father, destroy the hold of social media on my life in Jesus' name.
Father, help me to locate only the contents that will draw me closer to you.
Father, take over the social media space and show Your glory and power through it.
Father, use me as an agent of transformation on all platforms I find myself.
golden_diet: Guard your heart with all diligence.
You can be the change in the midst of filth.
Make it a duty for Jesus to be seen through you.
Trends are ephemeral but God is everlasting.
Change others but don't allow others to change you.
Plug out the noise and seek to hear from God.
Live every day with the consciousness of who you are.

weeks.memory_verse: “Train up a child in the way he should go; and when he is old, he will not depart from it. Proverbs 22:6
weeks.lesson_introduction: A child is expected to be a better version of his or her parents. Your child is supposed to be a new improved you, your child is your future hence losing your child to the devil amounts to losing your life while gaining your child is gaining your future. Never surrender your child to bad company or influence, guide and nurture him/her to become an improved version of you.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: FUTURE STARTS WITH SEED
outlines.body:
Many parents have destroyed their children's future based on the seed being planted from the cradle.
Children are divine investment in the future to be preserved for continuity. Psalm 127:3.
Neglecting children means neglecting your tomorrow.
What you plant in them, will be the results tomorrow.
Train your children in God's pattern in order to secure your legacy. Proverbs 22:6.
If you sow good character in your children, you will reap leaders.
Watch your children's exposure to screens; what are they seeing?
Teach them household chores, godly daily lifestyle, yank out laziness from them.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: HOW TO GUIDE CHILDREN
outlines.body:
Children are to be guided, don't leave them alone to themselves, be intentional in their wellbeing.
Spiritual foundation ensures children grow with purpose, wisdom and the fear of God.
Talent without godliness can destroy a beautiful future.
When a generation is not properly taught, darkness will take over.
Always lead by example, children learn more from what they see.
Teach your children early and consistently. Proverbs 22:6
Combine love with discipline. Allow them to ask questions and express emotions. James 1:19.
Guide their spiritual life and encourage your children. Ephesians 6:4.
Set boundaries and structure for your children. Proverbs 29:15

weeks.conclusion: Children are not just for today's joy, they are for tomorrow's leadership, innovation and spiritual strength. The future we desire must be intentionally built on them.
weeks.weekly_activity: Discuss the lapses of Eli in raising his children and the consequences.
prayer_points: Father, grant us wisdom and patience to raise godly children.
Father, plant Your fear, humility and divine virtues in my children.
Father, shield our children from ungodly associations.
Father, let Your word take deep roots in the lives of our children.
Father, give our children obedient hearts and ability to say no to sin.
golden_diet: All our children shall be taught of the Lord and great shall be their peace. Isaiah 54:13
Do not provoke your children to wrath. Ephesians 6:4
But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. Joshua 24:15.
Children are the heritage of the Lord. Psalm 127:34.
Blessed is the man whose quiver is full of children.
Teach your children diligently and plant moral values in them.
Never deprive your children of discipline.

Father, don't let any member of house fellowship unit miss your second coming.
Father, please send committed soul winners to harvest souls as your coming is nearer.
Father, continue to increase greatly in the ministry of Daddy and Mummy GO.
Father, revive our nation to become righteous nation.
golden_diet: Always see yourself as light over darkness
Put yourself in active kingdom work, night will soon come. John 9:4
Be obedient to divine instructions. 2 kings 5: 10, 15,
Testify to people of positive changes in your life. John 9:11.
Abstain from contamination that may terminate your new beginning. 1 Thess.5:22.
Always believe in divine presence and His influence. Hebrews 11:5.
Bear ye one another's burdens. Galatians 6:2

weeks.memory_verse: “Ye are of God, little children, have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world. 1 John 4:4
weeks.lesson_introduction: 1 John 4:4 tells us that regardless of our age, level, background, tribe, race, etc., the moment we become God's children, we will overcome whatever comes our way because we are God's children. The Lord dwell in us and He is greater than whatever problem or challenge that may come our way. As believers, we are called to be overcomers through faith in Christ, who has already secured our victory over the challenges of life.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: BECOMING AN OVERCOMER
outlines.body:
To become an overcomer is a decision every believer should make based on the word of God in 1 John 4:4. When you have made that decision, then you will work towards it by doing the following and many more:
Relationship with Jesus. Matthew 11:28.
Know who you are. Prov. 2:7. See yourself the way God sees you, don't give room for doubt. Jas 1:7.
Intimacy with God. James 4:8. You cannot operate as an overcomer without intimacy with Him.
Believe and declare the word. Numbers 14:28. Rev.12:11, Colossians 2:13-15.
Act on the Word. Hebrew 10:38.
Use your authority. Luke 10:19.
Stand in faith. Ephesians 6:13-16.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: CHARACTERISTICS OF AN OVERCOMER
outlines.body:
The scriptures tell us that a tree is known by its fruits. Likewise, overcomers are known by the character and attitude they display anytime and wherever there are challenges. Some of the characteristics are:
Faith in Jesus Christ. Daniel 11:32, Hebrews 10:38.
Endurance through trials. Overcomers demonstrate resilience in the face of adversity. James 1:12.
Recognizing ones identity in Christ. Romans 8:37, 1 John 5:4.
Viewing challenges as stepping stones, opportunities for growth rather than obstacles. John 13:15.

weeks.conclusion: Every believer has been given the authority to overcome all the challenges and tribulations of the world. John 16:33. The extent of your victories will be determined by how much your faith, the power you draw from Jesus. Matthew 28:18, the source of all power in your daily devotion, prayer life and obedience. John 5:39, John 14:13-14, 2 Corinthians 10:6.
weeks.weekly_activity: Discuss five biblical characters that showed confidence in God in times of tribulations.
prayer_points: Father, thank You for making me an overcomer.
Father, I make up my mind to walk with You daily, please help me to be faithful.
Father, reveal Yourself to me daily as I study your word.
Father, equip me with power to overcome the obstacles on my path to victory.
Father, make my life a testimony of Your completed work at Calvary.
golden_diet: For everyone born of God overcomes the world. 1 John 5:4
No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us. Romans 8:37
In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world. John 16:33.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. Philippians 4:13.
Not by might nor power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord Almighty. Zechariah 4:6
If God is for us, who can be against us?
No weapon formed against you shall prosper. Isaiah 54:17

weeks.opening_prayer: Father, please bless and keep me all the days of my life.

weeks.memory_verse: “I can do all things through Christ which strengthens me” Philippians 4:13
weeks.lesson_introduction: In Zechariah 2:8, God declared that we are the apple of His eyes and His heritage, whatever untoward affects us affects our God and He will rise to solve the problem. Hebrews 4:15. Isaiah 49:16 tells us that He has engraved us in the palm of His hands. What God needs from us is to know how dear we are to Him and trust Him to shower us with His love. Proverbs 3:5-6, Isaiah 26:4, Psalm 121:7-8. As we trust and hold on Him, we will continually enjoy His favour and blessings in every area of our lives. Numbers 6:24-26.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: HUMAN STRENGTH FAILS
outlines.body:
Defeat of Israel by Ai in Joshua 7 shows us that human might can fail.
When there is sin in the camp of believers defeat is inevitable.
When you have divine presence, the giant must fall. 1 Samuel 17.
It does not matter how tough, big, strong the enemy or the problem is, when God backs you up, you will laugh. Zechariah 4:6-7.
Eyes of Most High watch over His children to defend, fight their battles, provide for them and bless them. Exodus 14:14, Isaiah 41:10-13.
Believers are to accomplish their tasks and fulfil their destinies since God's presence is with them.
We are special heritage of our God. 1 Peter 2:9, Philippians 4:13.
Human being's ability is limited but God is limitless. Psalm 108:12.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: UNDERSTANDING GOD'S STRENGTH AND BENEFITS
outlines.body:
Understanding His strength is not just about knowing that He's powerful, it is about experiencing His power in our lives on daily basis, because we will always encounter challenges that test our physical, emotion, financial and intellectual capacity. To understand and enjoy the benefits of God's strength, we must know the following;
God's strength is eternal and unshaking. Isaiah 40:28. Daniel 11:32
God renews our strength when we are weary. Isaiah 40:31
His strength is the refuge in times of trouble. Psalm 46:1
That there is provision of peace in the midst of chaos. John 14:27.
There is boldness and courage to confront obstacles and challenges. 2 Timothy 1:7, Joshua 1:9.

weeks.conclusion: God's strength is not just a concept, it is a living reality for those who trust Him. When we acknowledge our weakness, lean on his power, and walk in faith, we experience a life of resilience, peace and victory.
weeks.weekly_activity: Discuss vivid biblical example of human strength that failed
prayer_points: Father, thank you for Your inexhaustible power and strength.
Father, thank you for choosing me as your heritage, let your favour surround me as shield.
Father, thank you for your numerous blessings available to me as your heritage.
Father, wherever I am help me to always rely on you.
Father, teach my hands to prosper, make the head always.
golden_diet: No king is saved by the size of his army. Psalm 33:16-17.
Cursed is the one who trusts in man, who draws strength from mere flesh. Jeremiah 17:5.
Give us aid against the enemy, for human help is worthless. Psalm 60:11.
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help. Isaiah 31:1.
By strength shall no man prevail. 1 Samuel 2:9.
With him is only the arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God. 2 Chronicles 32:8.
Do not put your trust in princes, in human beings, who cannot save. Psalm 146:3

weeks.memory_verse: “For their god is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame” Philippians 3:19
weeks.lesson_introduction: Appetite is not evil if it is positive and not character damaging or bringing insults to the body of Christ but lack of control is the problem. Uncontrolled appetite has destroyed destinies, homes, etc.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: UNDERSTANDING APPETITE AND TYPES
outlines.body:
Appetite is a strong desire for pleasure, power, attention, food and approval. Proverbs 16:32 says he that ruleth his spirit is better than he that taketh a city.
Examples of uncontrolled appetite;
Esau. It caused him birthright. Genesis 25:29-34.
Samson sold his strength, glory and his calling to indiscipline and insatiable quest for sex. Judges 16.
Adam and Eve's desire for what God forbid caused them their inheritance. Genesis 3:6.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: TYPES OF APPETITE AND DANGERS OF NOT CONTROLLING
outlines.body:
There are uncontrolled appetite;
Physical - Proverbs 23:20-21. Gluttony leads to sickness and laziness.
Emotional - Seeking attention, depending on people. Jeremiah 17:5.
Spiritual - having junks as food will lead to unfulfilled dreams. Matthew 4:4
WHAT ARE THE DANGERS OF UNCONTROLLED APPETITE?
Loss of destiny and weakness in prayer life.
Broken relationship.
Spiritual imprisonment.
Shame and Regret. Adam and Eve were sent out of garden of Eden.

weeks.conclusion: Developing self-discipline, practicing spiritual exercise and feeding on undiluted word of God will reduce craving for fleshy things. Set boundaries on your appetite.
weeks.weekly_activity: What are the virtues uncontrolled appetite can withdraw from the captives?
prayer_points: Father, deliver me from destructive appetite.
Holy Spirit, empower me to walk in self-control.
Every appetite fighting my destiny be subdued.
I receive grace to hunger for righteousness.
golden_diet: Like a city whose walls are broken through is a person who lacks self-control. Proverbs 25:28
The destiny of victim of uncontrolled appetite is destruction. Philippians 3:19.
Put a knife to your throat if you are given to gluttony. Proverbs 23:2.
Walk in the Spirit and you will not fulfil the desires of the flesh. Galatians 5:16.
Make no provision for the flesh. Romans 13:14.
Abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. 1 Peter 2:11
I discipline my body and bring it unto subjection. 1 Corinthians 9:27

weeks.memory_verse: “Blessed are the peacemakers; for they shall be called children of God” Matthew 5:9
weeks.lesson_introduction: Peace is not the absence of trouble or discontentment, it is the presence of God navigating His influence of establishing God's order. God does not only call us to have peace, but to make peace. A peace maker is not weak but a Christ inspired being.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: PEACEMAKER
outlines.body:
A peacemaker is the one who;
Promotes reconciliation. Exodus 32:11-14
Stops strife, not spreads it.
Restores broken relationships. Luke 23:34
Reflects God's nature of peace over nations. Genesis 13, 18.
Speaks truth in love. Ephesians 4:15.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: QUALITIES OF A TRUE PEACEMAKER
outlines.body:
Pure and gentle. James 3:17-18.
Easy to be entreated.
Full of mercy.
Controls their tongue. Proverbs 15:1
Walks in humility. Proverbs 13:10.
Chooses forgiveness. Colossians 3:13

weeks.conclusion: Peacemakers are called children of God, enjoys divine favor, experiences peace and releases healing in families, communities, churches and nations. Psalm 34:14.
weeks.weekly_activity: What are the dangers of dwelling in rancourous atmosphere?
prayer_points: Father, make me an instrument of your peace.
Every spirit of strife in my life, be uprooted.
Grace to forgive and reconcile, rest upon me.
Let peace reign in my home and nation.
Lord, increase the strength and your grace on Daddy and Mummy GO.
golden_diet: Blessed are the peacemakers for they shall be called children of God. Matthew 5:9.
If it is possible as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone. Romans 12:18.
Make every effort to live in peace with everyone and to be holy. Hebrews 12:14.
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger. Proverbs 15:1
Bear with each other and forgive each other. Colossians 3:13-15.
Be completely humble and gentle, be patient bearing with one another. Ephesians 4:2-3
Turn from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it. Psalm 34:14.

weeks.memory_verse: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witness, let us lay aside every weight and the sin which doth so easily beset us and let us run with patience the race that is before us” Hebrew 12:1.
weeks.lesson_introduction: We live in an age of abundance - abundant information, choices, demands on our time and attention. Our lives often feel overflowing, overscheduled and overwhelmed. Just as a write edits a manuscript, a filmmaker edits footage, or a gardener prunes a plant we need a process of editing our lives.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: NEED FOR DIVINE EDIT
outlines.body:
There is a saying that when a man recognizes and acknowledges that he has a problem, the problem is half solved, when we have clutter in our lives, it needs to be edited.
A clutter is a collection of things lying about in an untidy state, our heart can be room that is cluttered. This obvious clutter- habits, attitudes, relationship that pull us away from God. These are not just distractions, they are hindrance. Good things can hinder like good activities too much comfort, good relationship can deprive God's relationship, good causes, or even good intentions can become clutter if they distract us from our primary calling or exhaust us to the point of spiritual depletion. Martha's dilemma in Luke 10:38-42.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: SYMPTOMS OF A CLUTTERED LIFE
outlines.body:
Feeling constantly busy but rarely productive in what truly matters.
Spiritual dryness or inconsistency.
Emotional exhaustion, anxiety or resentment.
Lack of peace and clarity.
Difficulty hearing God's voice.
We are to fix our eyes on Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of faith. Hebrews 12:2. He is the ultimate example of a life perfectly edited, perfectly focused on the Father's will

weeks.conclusion: What is one area of your life where you sense God is calling for edit this week? Invite God into that space, ask him to show you what needs to be thrown off like Jonah so that boat of your life won't sink.
weeks.weekly_activity: Set a day apart this week for thorough examination of yourself.
prayer_points: Father, purge my heart from hypocrisy, pride and hidden sin.
Father, surround me with godly and visionary friends and associates.
Lord, let my life, service and labour receive your approval and not rejection.
Father, banish from me glory draining adventures and associates.
Lord, fill Daddy and Mummy GO with fresh anointing and keep on renewing them.
golden_diet: Examine me Lord and try me test my mind and my heart. Psalm 26:2
Let us examine our ways and test them and let us return to the Lord. Lamentation 3:40.
For we must all appear before the judgement seat of Christ. 2 Corinthians 5:10.
Behold The Lord is coming quickly with His rewards. Revelation 22:12
So then each of us will give account of himself. Romans 14:12.
Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the heart. Proverbs 21:2
Many have been weighed in the balances and found wanting. Daniel 5:27

weeks.week_heading: WEEK FORTY FIVE - THANKSGIVING SUNDAY, 4TH JULY, 2027.
weeks.memory_verse: “But seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness and all these things shall be added unto you. Matthew 6:33” Hebrew 12:1
weeks.lesson_introduction: Last week we examined divine edit part one, focusing on the need to remove the clutter that fills our lives and the signs of a cluttered life. Today we will be explore the practical steps of a cluttered life and the tools needed for editing.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: PRACTICAL EVIDENCE IN A CLUTTERED LIFE
outlines.body:
Looking at 1 kings 19:13 and Luke 15:11-32, these are steps of a cluttered life;
Unused or abandoned virtues. 1 Corinthians 14:40.
Overthinking and worry
Unresolved decisions, negative thoughts and self-doubt.
Lack of focus. Philippians 4:8.
Unforgiveness, past hurts, guilt and shame. Hebrews 12:1
Over commitment, poor time management and saying yes to everything.
No clear priority.
Neglecting prayer altar, religious activities without relationship

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: EDITOR'S TOOLS
outlines.body:
Jesus Christ is the divine editor, when we surrender to Him, He will edit our lives to fulfil His purpose. So let us glue our eyes to Him to effect positive transformation in our lives. Hebrews 12:2
The word of God. Hebrews 4:12. His word will help us to discern between good, better and the best.
The Holy Spirit. The Spirit convicts, guides and illuminates. He brings clarity to confusion.
Prayer and solitude. This is our editing session in quiet moment, laying our lives before God.
Wise Counsel. Sometimes God uses trusted mentors, pastors or friends to help us see the clutter we have become blind to. Exodus 18:2'

weeks.summary: When our lives are being edited, it's not about making our lives empty but making them full of what truly matters. It's about freedom, focus and fruitfulness, it's about running the race marked out for us with perseverance.
weeks.conclusion: A cluttered life drains energy, blocks progress and steals peace, let divine editor work on you. Avoid toxic relationship, unnecessary conflicts and unhealthy boundary
weeks.weekly_activity: What are the boundaries you ought to set to avoid cluttering?
prayer_points: Father, grant me peace that silences every noise and confusion in my mind.
O Lord deliver me from anxiety, fear and mental overload and restore my sound mind.
I cast out everything cluttering my thought hindering me from hearing God's voice
Every negative harmful, unproductive thought pattern in my mind be uprooted.
Father, align my thought with your will.
golden_diet: Set your mind on things above not on things on the earth. Colossians 3:2.
For God is not an author of confusion but of peace. 1 Corinthians 14:55
Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid. John 14:27.
You will keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you. Isaiah 26:3.
Be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind. Romans 12:2.
And the peace of God which surpasses all understanding will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. Philippians 4:7
God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love and sound mind. 2 Timothy 1:7

weeks.memory_verse: “Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard lest at any time we should let them slip” Hebrew 2:1
weeks.lesson_introduction: Carelessness is acting without attention, discipline or reverence. Many people lose great things in life not because of Satan alone but because they are careless. Spiritual gifts, marriages, opportunities, health and destiny have been lost through carelessness.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: CARELESSNESS
outlines.body:
A little yeast can be like carelessness does not shout, it whispers. It starts small but ends big.
Samson was careless with his consecration and paid for it. Judges 16:17-21.
Esau was careless with his birthright, he paid with groaning. Genesis 25:34.
Eli was careless with discipline his sons, lost his ministry and lost them one day. 1 Samuel 2:29-30.
Carelessness opens doors to losses, weakens spiritual life and ruin destiny. Matthew 26:41
Don't be careless with your prayer, bible study and consecration life. Never allow your lamp to go out.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: HOW TO AVOID CARELESS LIVING?
outlines.body:
Stay alert spiritually. 1 Peter 5:8
Value instruction and correction. Proverbs 12:1.
Imbibe godly living. 1 Timothy 4:16.
Put God first in your decisions. Eccl. 12:13.
Avoid gathering of careless people. Proverbs 1:10
Examine your life regularly. 2 Corinthians 13:5

weeks.conclusion: God rewards careful living. Learn from Joseph that ran away from being careless with his service at Potiphar's house. Proverbs 4:23, 1 Corinthians 15:58
weeks.weekly_activity: Discuss other biblical characters that were careless and the consequences.
prayer_points: Father, deliver me from every form of spiritual carelessness.
Father, guide my thought and decisions.
I reject any careless step that can lead me to give regret.
Father, help me to value and maximize opportunity.
Lord, deliver me from a careless prayer life, help me to remain consistent and devoted.
golden_diet: Give earnest attention to thing you have heard so as not to slip from them. Hebrews 2:1.
Be sober, be vigilant because your adversary the devil walks about to devour. 1 Peter 5:8
The simple believes every word, but the prudent considers well his steps. Proverbs 14:15.
See then that you walk circumspectly, redeeming the time. Ephesians 5:16
Fear God and keep His commandments.
For God has not given us the spirit of fear but of power love and a sound mind. 2 Timothy 1:7
Catch us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vines. Song of Solomon 2:15.

weeks.memory_verse: “Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken and we are escaped” Psalm 124:7
weeks.lesson_introduction: Promotion can come to you either human or divine assistance. The assisted state of progress attained through this promotion moves you to the next level you are not supposed to be, may the Lord in this season assist you and move you to a level you are not qualified to occupy in Jesus name.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: ACTIONS TO ACTIVATE GOD KIND OF PROGRESS
outlines.body:
Progress with speed does not mean rushing blindly it means carrying out actions to activate it.
Align with God's plan and mandate.
Be diligent, consistent and be obedience. Proverbs 21:5, Proverbs 22:29.
Activate faith for acceleration. Matthew 17:20.
Remove barriers that can slow you down.
Always hunger for more. God satisfy hungry souls.
Have visions and plans. Hab.2:3

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: DANGERS OF BEING STAGNANT
outlines.body:
Where there is no vision, people will perish. Let us look at dangers of stagnation.
It makes believer weak and vulnerable. Lot was weak in Sodom. Genesis 19.
There will be missed opportunities. Ecclesiastes 11:4.
Loss of influence. Matthew 5:13.
Lack of spiritual growth makes believer vulnerable to temptation.
Stagnation prevents one from fulfilling destiny. Jeremiah 29:11

weeks.conclusion: God does not want us to just move slowly, He desires accelerated advancement in our lives being stagnant is even dangerous
weeks.key_note: God wants you not just move forward but move forward swiftly.
prayer_points: Father, I refuse stagnation, accelerate my progress.
Father, open doors of new opportunity for me in this year.
Lord, cut off every delay and limitation in my life, remove all obstacles on my path.
Father, strengthen Daddy and Mummy GO to walk diligently and remain consistent to divine call
Lord, let your favour lift me to the next level.
golden_diet: Forgetting what is behind reaching for what is before. Philippians 3:13-14.
But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn. Proverbs 4:18.
God has promised to make you head and not tail. Deut. 28:13
The least of you shall become a thousand and the smallest a mighty nation. Isaiah 60:22
Promotion and progress is divinely orchestrated. Psalm 75:6-7
For God's plans require growth, action and movement.
Remaining stagnant delays your blessings and breakthroughs.

weeks.memory_verse: “She said, no man Lord. And Jesus said unto her, neither do I condemn thee: go and sin no more” John 8:11
weeks.lesson_introduction: Sin is primarily any act that is against the laws, will, plan and purpose of God which encompasses our actions, our thoughts, words and omissions. Our God is pure and cannot tolerate sin. Hab. 1:13, Isaiah 59:1-2. Whenever we commit sin, we are challenging the Lordship of God over our lives and submitting to the ownership and authority of the devil over our lives. John 8:44, 1 John 3:8. Therefore, as children of God, we are expected to run away from sin. 1 Thessalonians 5:22 so that we can continue to enjoy the benefits of our sonship. However, when we fall into sin and we repent, God is merciful and will forgive us and restore us back to Himself. Proverbs 28:11

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: GOD IS MERCIFUL. Psalm 103:8
outlines.body:
His great love and compassion makes Him to release His mercy. Lam. 3:23.
His mercy brings forgiveness of sin. Ephesians 2:4-5.
God even feels our pains, shame and reproach. Psalm 34:18.
His mercy overrules any form of judgement.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: MERCY, NOT A LICENSE TO SIN
outlines.body:
Mercy is not a license to sin rather God releases His mercy to give you another opportunity to consider your ways, repent and return to Him. Jeremiah 3:22, Romans 6:1.
God's grace to overcome sin is released upon every Christian. 2 Corinthians 12:9, it is also sufficient to overcome all temptations of sin and to work out our salvation. Philippians 2:12. As Christians, God's mercy and grace makes us;
Free from hold of sin. Romans 6:14.
Possesses seed of righteousness. James 3:18.
This seed of righteousness enables us to obey God's word and His instructions. Ephesians 5:6-10.
We are alive to God. Galatians 2:19-20.
God's grace enables us to run away from sin and to please God in everything we do. 1 Thess. 5:22

weeks.conclusion: Sin is a destroyer of man because it leads to spiritual separation from God Isaiah 59:1-2 and without God man is useless. God's mercy is available to cleanse us from every form of sin and as we receive God's forgiveness and cleansing we are to run from anything that will make us fall into sin. 2 Corin. 5:17
weeks.weekly_activity: What are causes of Demas' quitting God's service?
prayer_points: Father, I surrender my all to you please cleanse me from all unrighteousness
Father, please sanctify my heart by your blood and your word of truth.
Father, by your grace I will overcome the temptations of sin.
Father, please sow the seeds of righteousness in my heart.
Father, I promise to live my life to please You.
golden_diet: Be very careful on how you live, make most of every opportunity. Ephesians 5:15-16.
Do not conform to the pattern of this world. Romans 12:2
Set examples for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love. 1 Timothy 4:12
Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds. Matthew 5:16
Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase? Romans 6:1-2.
Therefore there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. Romans 8:1-2
Do not allow sin to reign in your mortal body so that you obey its evil desires. Romans 6:12

weeks.topic: LOVE, THE FRUIT OF HOLY SPIRIT
weeks.memory_verse: “and now abideth faith, hope, charity, these, but the greatest of these is charity” 1 Corin. 13:13
weeks.lesson_introduction: Love is the fruit of the Holy Spirit, Galatians 5:22. When we love, it is evidence that the Spirit of God lives in us, 1 John 4:13, 16. He enables us to love like God loves. God manifested His love by sending Jesus Christ as a sacrifice to take away our sins. If God loves us this much, we ought to love each other not by our power but by power of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. Anyone who loves is a child of God but anyone who does not love does not belong to God, for God is love. 1 John 4:7-8

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: LOVE PERSONIFIED
outlines.body: God is love, He manifested His love in the Person of Jesus Christ to us. God sent His only begotten Son, Our Lord Jesus Christ to die for our sins - this is love personified. 1 John 3:9. When we receive God's love we receive the gift of eternal life. For God so loved us that He gave Jesus Christ to save us from our sins and free us from death. Whosoever believes in Him shall not perish but have everlasting life, John 3:16. When we confess that Jesus is the Son of God, we know and believe the love God has for us. 1 John 4:15-16. We become one in God - we dwell in God and God dwells in us and nothing shall be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord. Romans 8:7-39.

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: ESSENTIALS OF LOVE
outlines.body:
God's love comprises of essentials which shows that the Holy Spirit is the Source. Hence the title of our lesson, love, the fruit of the Spirit. We find essentials of love in the Word of God.
Love is patient and kind. 1 Corinthians 13:4
Love is not envious or jealous, proud or rude, provoked or thinks evil. 1 Corinthians 13:4-5
Love is neither irritable nor keeps record of being wronged. 1 Corinthians 13:5.
Love rejoices in truth not in injustice. 1 Corinthians 13:6.
Love never fails, is always hopeful, full of faith and lasts forever. 1 Corinthians 13:7.
Love gives and is not self-seeking - 1 John 4:10.
Love does not fear. 1 John 4:18.
Love does not hate. 1 John 4:20.

weeks.conclusion: Loving others is the evidence we must show that we know God and His Spirit dwells in us. If you say you love God but hate your brother, you lie. If you do not love your brother who you see, how can you love God who you have not seen? 1 John 4:20. God commands us to love one another as He has loved us.
weeks.weekly_activity: What are the practical ways of loving others?
prayer_points: Father, fill my heart with Your divine love through the Holy Spirit.
Lord, remove every hardness and bitterness from my heart.
Lord, let love govern my reactions and responses.
Every root of offense in my heart, be uprooted in Jesus Name.
Lord, make me a vessel through which Your love flows to others.
golden_diet: But the fruit of the Spirit of love, joy , peace, long suffering, gentleness, goodness, Galatians 5:22
He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love. 1 John 4:8
Love poured by The Holy Spirit. Romans 5:5.
Love as the greatest Christian virtue. 1 Corinthians 13:13.
Love as evidence of true discipleship. John 13:34-35.

weeks.memory_verse: “Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan” 1 kings 17:3
weeks.lesson_introduction: It is wisdom to obey when He instruct you to hide. Known unto God are all His works from the foundation of the world. He will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are stayed on Him because they trust in Him, Isaiah 26:3. There is time for everything, Ecclesiastes 3:1-11. Our Bible text shows us that God the Father instructed Joseph to hide our Lord Jesus Christ from Herod who sought to kill Him. Joseph obeyed God's instruction that Herod was dead, Matthew 2:19-20. When God hides you, you must remain in hiding and obediently wait for your time of showing.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: THERE IS TIME TO HIDE
outlines.body:
We see through scriptures that there is time a to hide. There are several accounts in the bible where God instructed people to hide and those who obeyed Him were preserved. Some examples are:
1. In the days of Noah, God commanded Noah and His family to enter the ark to preserve them from destruction. Genesis 7:1
2. He commanded the children of Israel to hide in their houses marked with blood on the lintel while the destroyer passed over their houses. Exodus 12:23.
3. He commanded Elijah to hide in a place to be fed during a famine. 1 kings 17:2-3.
4. He commanded Joseph to hide the child Jesus Christ until those who sought to kill him were dead. Matthew 2:13-20.

There were also accounts in the Bible where God gave people wisdom to either hide or hide others from danger and they were preserved. Examples are:
Rahab hid the two spies. Joshua 2:3-15.
David hid from King Saul. 1 Samuel 22:1
Obadiah hid one hundred prophets. 1 kings 18:4
Mordecai hid Esther's identity. Esther 2:10.
Lot and his family were removed from destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. Genesis 19:15-22
Israelites were hidden in Goshen from plagues. Exodus 8:22, 9:26, 10:23

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: TIME TO HIDE IS GOD'S PEROGATIVE
outlines.body:
Timing is in God's hands, He is the righteous judge. Genesis 18:25.
God hides people only at His appointed time. Isaiah 26:20.
God's action is effected when His plan is completed. Genesis 7:1. Preparation is man's responsibility, timing is God's authority.
Deliverance will surely come at the appointed time. Exodus 12:41.
Early or late movement in action can lead to destruction. Numbers 14:42-45.
Acting outside God's timing - even with good intentions - leads to loss.
God's protection operates by divine schedule. Ecclesiastes 3:1. There is time to stay, hide and escape

weeks.conclusion: God's prerogative is not just to save, but to decide when salvation is activated. Come my people enter thou into thy chambers and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment until the indignation be overpast. Isaiah 26:20
weeks.weekly_activity: What are the ways and when is the time children of God can discern that it is time to hide?
prayer_points: Father, thank you for teaching us that there is time to hide.
Father, please keep me in Your secret place in Jesus Name.
Father, please hide me under the shadow of Your wings.
Father, reveal to Your children when it is time to hide and show them how to stay safe in Jesus Name.
Father, please keep our parents in the Lord as the apple of Your eyes and hide them under the shadow of your wings in Jesus name.
golden_diet: When trouble comes, God activates divine hiding. Psalm 27:5.
God hides you during indignation and judgement. Isaiah 26:20.
When destruction is announced, God hides the righteous. Job 5:21.
When humanity hostility rises, God hides His people. Psalm 31:20.
When pestilences, terror, and danger increase, divine covering is released. Psalm 91:L1-4.
When famine and persecution arise, God hides His servants. 1 kings 17:3-4.
God hides His chosen until their time. Colossians 3:3

weeks.memory_verse: “The wicked are overthrown, and are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.” Proverbs 12:7
weeks.lesson_introduction: The righteous keeps the way of the Lord to do justice and judgement and this is more acceptable of the Lord than sacrifice, Proverbs 21:3. Abraham became a mighty nation, and all nations of the earth are blessed in him just as the Lord promised because God judged him faithful. Romans 4:17-18. God blessed Abraham because He knew Abraham will teach his children to live righteously, to do justice and judgement. This was the guarantee that God's blessing will continue from generation to generation, Genesis 18:19. Justice and judgement are the habitation of God, Psalm 89:14. Therefore God dwells in the home of the righteous.

outlines.label: One
outlines.title: WHAT MAKES A HOME RIGHTEOUS?
outlines.body:
God dwells in the home of the righteous. John 14:23.
The word of God is taught and obeyed. Genesis 18:19
The parents teach their children the word of God. Deuteronomy 6:7.
The father walks in integrity and his children are blessed after him. Proverbs 20:7.
The husband loves his wife and is not bitter against her. Colossians 3:19.
The wife submits to her husband as it is fit in the Lord. Colossians 3:18.
The children obey their parents in all things: for this is well pleasing in the Lord. Colossians 3:20.
The father does not provoke his children lest they be discouraged. Col 3:21.
The workers serve heartly with sincerity and in the fear of the Lord Acts 9:31, Colossians 3:22.
The blessing and favour of God. Psalm 5:12

outlines.label: Two
outlines.title: BLESSINGS OF HOME OF THE RIGHTEOUS
outlines.body:
The presence of God dwells there. Proverbs 3:33.
They enjoy calmness, order and divine stability. Isaiah 32:18.
Evil plans and destructive forces are restrained by God's edge. Psalm 121:7.
God supplies needs and blesses the work of their hands. Proverbs 15:6.
Children and descendants benefit from the righteousness of the parents. Psalm 112:2.
The atmosphere of the home is filled with gladness and thanksgiving. Proverbs 29:6.
The home is preserved and established over time. Proverbs 12:7

weeks.conclusion: Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, the Lord knoweth them that are His. And, let everyone that nameth the Name of Christ depart from iniquity. 2 Timothy 2:19
weeks.weekly_activity: Discuss how parents can practically ensure their children are taught the word of God.
prayer_points: Father, thank you for teaching us that the home of the righteous is blessed and that righteousness is profitable.
Father, help me to live righteously and walk before You in integrity.
Father, teach me to number my days and apply my heart unto wisdom.
Father, give all parents the wisdom to train their children in Your way in Jesus name.
Father, let our parents in the Lord enjoy the rewards of their labour of love over us.
golden_diet: The home of the righteous will stand. Proverbs 12:7
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright. Psalm 112:4
The home of the righteous is associated with honour and godly influence. Proverbs 10:7
My people will live in peaceful dwelling places in secure homes, undisturbed places of rest.
God blesses the home of the righteous and curse the home of the wicked. Proverbs 3:33
They enjoy calmness, order and divine stability. Isaiah 32:18.

weeks.overview:
LOVE FEAST/ THANKSGIVING/ EVALUATION OF THE JUST ENDED YEAR AND DELIBERATIONS ON HOW TO MOVE OUR CENTERS FORWARD.
a. Leader and member should discuss challenges confronting the centre.
b. Suggestions that can foster growth of house fellowship.
c. The materials used this year, what is of quality or not?
d. Is the environment where the centre is conducive or manageable?
e. Center should organize love feast.
The leader should write down suggestion for review and later bless centre members
prayer_points: Father, thank you for carrying us through another RCCG calendar year.
Lord, as another RCCG year ends, everything assigned to end my year in shame be silenced.
Every last minute sorrow, evil agenda is cancelled over my life.
O God of completion complete every good thing you started in my life.
What was delayed shall be released, what was pending for me shall be settled.
golden_diet: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning. Ecclesiastes 7:8. God specializes in strong endings.
He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion. Philippians 1:6
They that wait on the Lord shall renew their strength. Isaiah 40:31.
And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten. Joel 2:25.
Though thy beginning was small, yet thy later end should greatly increase. Job 8:7
The Lord hath done great things for us.... Psalm 126:3
The path of the just is as the shining light. Proverbs 4:18
